To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Chinese construction project managers conceive of project management competence as: a) a combination of knowledge, skills, and attitudes; b) a combination of technical and non-technical competencies; c) a combination of hard and soft skills; d) a combination of project management and construction knowledge; e) the ability to manage the project in accordance with the project management standards; and f) a combination of the ability to manage a project and to manage the people involved in the project.
the conceptual determinants for construction project management competence in the Chinese context are similar to those found in the previous UK study.
the Chinese construction project managers conceive and perform their work in three different ways: as a technical problem, as an organizational issue and as a personal challenge.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the conceptual determinants, rather than the content of construction project management knowledge, and is thus different from other research on the content of construction management knowledge and its transferability.
the conceptual determinants and practical implications of the construction project management competence in the Chinese context.
the question of what it means to project managers to be competent in managing construction projects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

construction project management competence in the Chinese context is conceptualized as: (1) a set of project-specific knowledge and skills that are required to accomplish the tasks and duties of a project manager; (2) a set of generic knowledge and skills, which are required to accomplish tasks and duties in different projects, and (3) a set of knowledge and skills that can be used to manage projects effectively.

the Chinese construction project managers conceive of and accomplish their work in a way that is similar to their UK counterparts, with a few differences that are attributable to the different national and organizational contexts.
the Chinese project managers’ conceptions of project management competence are similar to their counterparts in the UK, but are more likely to be influenced by their cultural and social background.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to achieve effective training and professional recognition of project management competence, it is important to understand the conceptual determinants and the ways in which project managers conceive and accomplish their work in different national contexts.
the Western project management standards and certification schemes are not a universal panacea to improve the quality of Chinese construction projects.
the Western standards-based project management competence is not the only way to conceive and accomplish construction project management competence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conceptual determinants are not culturally specific and that the phenomenographic approach has a potential to be used in cross-cultural studies.

the conceptual determinants revealed in this study are likely to be relevant in other contexts where project management is practiced, but the ways in which they are manifested in the work of project managers are context-specific and need to be explored empirically.
project management competence is a socially constructed concept, and its conceptualisation is context-specific and culturally determined.
